scenes.title: 1937 Montreal Teaching Suite: Wilder Penfield's Numbered Cortical Ticket Model Beside the Giant-Handed Porcelain Homunculus Sculpture

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1937 Montreal neurological teaching amphitheater featuring an oak demonstration table holding a large matte-white 3D anatomical cerebral hemisphere dotted along the central sulcus with tiny **sterile numbered white paper tickets ('1, 2, 3 ... 14')**, a fine silver bipolar stimulation wand, and a museum-grade **matte-white porcelain Homunculus sculpture** with oversized hands, thumbs, and lips.

positions.who: Wilder Penfield (mannequin in crisp 1937 white surgical/clinical coat)
positions.where: touching numbered ticket #14 on the matte-white motor-strip brain model with a fine silver probe while pointing to the matching oversized thumb on the porcelain Homunculus sculpture

positions.who: Edwin Boldrey & Hortense Cantlie (mannequins in 1937 lab coat and artist smock)
positions.where: cross-checking the 126-patient cortical dot ledger against the hand-inked Homunculus proportion chart

props.name: matte-white 3D brain cast with numbered sterile paper tickets ('1–28') & bipolar probe
props.period_detail: reconstructs Penfield's iconic Montreal numbered-ticket mapping in clean gallery style
props.physical_behavior: exact clinical signature of the Montreal Procedure

props.name: sculpted matte-white porcelain Homunculus figure (giant hands/thumbs & lips, miniature torso)
props.period_detail: makes cortical magnification instantly unforgettable at a glance
props.physical_behavior: iconic museum sculpture inspired by Penfield, Boldrey & Cantlie

actions.verb_sequence: places numbered paper ticket #14 onto the lateral motor strip model -> points directly from ticket #14 to the giant porcelain thumb and ticket #22 to the oversized lips
unrolls the 1937 cortical-proportion cross-section chart beside the 126-case tally ledger

reactions.reaction: verify why human thumbs and speech organs occupy over half the strip
notes overlapping finger mosaics alongside the summary diagram

scenes.wardrobe: 1937 Montreal clinical coats over shirt and tie; 1930s illustrator smock over collared blouse.
scenes.recognition_hook: Scale a human figure to how much brain cortex each body part commands, and two giant toolmaking hands plus a speaking mouth dwarf the entire body.

key_visual.description: a 1937 neurological teaching table displaying a matte-white 3D brain model tagged with tiny numbered paper tickets beside a matte-white porcelain Homunculus sculpture with giant hands and lips

scenes.title: Two-Point Caliper Self-Test: Fingertip (2 mm) vs Back (40 mm)

layout.description: Bright sunlit table where a two-point blunt wooden caliper touches a fingertip vs upper shoulder.

positions.where: feeling two points clearly at 2 mm on the index fingertip while 30 mm apart on the back still feels like ONE single point!

props.name: blunt wooden two-point discrimination caliper
props.period_detail: lets anyone feel their own Homunculus magnification in 5 seconds

actions.verb_sequence: touches 2-mm caliper to index pad ('Two points!') -> touches 30-mm caliper to upper back ('Only one!')

reactions.reaction: laughs feeling their giant thumb cortex vs tiny back cortex directly

scenes.recognition_hook: Two toothpick tips 2 millimetres apart feel clearly separate on your fingertip — put them 30 millimetres apart on your back and your brain swears there is only one!

scenes.title: Modern Awake Violinist Mapping: Saving Music in the OR

layout.description: High-key sunlit clinical room where a violinist plays a clean melodic phrase while numbered cortical map points protect hand dexterity.

positions.where: verifying smooth left-hand finger vibrato across every mapped millimetre

props.name: violin & numbered digital cortical ticket map
props.period_detail: direct living legacy of Penfield's 1937 Montreal Procedure

actions.verb_sequence: plays swift scale cleanly while surgeon marks protected hand-mosaic boundary

scenes.recognition_hook: Every time a modern surgeon maps an awake guitarist or violinist to save their craft, they use Wilder Penfield's 1937 Montreal ticket method.

scenes.title: 2023 Nature Rewrite: Three Mind-Body 'SCAN' Hubs Inside Motor Cortex

layout.description: Clean neuroimaging display comparing the 1937 continuous ribbon against the 2023 concentric Foot / Hand / Mouth bullseyes interleaved with three purple/amber SCAN nodes.

positions.where: pointing to the three interleaved whole-body SCAN nodes connecting prefrontal goals to posture and heart rate

props.name: 1937 Classic Ribbon vs 2023 SCAN Interleaved Map display
props.period_detail: biggest update to Penfield's motor map in 86 years

actions.verb_sequence: highlights the three SCAN bridges between Foot, Hand, and Mouth zones

reactions.reaction: spot the exact same mixed points hiding inside Penfield's original 1937 raw tickets!

scenes.recognition_hook: After 86 years in every textbook, 2023 precision MRI found three whole-body mind-body planning hubs tucked right inside Penfield's motor strip!
